The Drift Jar

A finite jar of gold and slate. Nothing selects, nothing mutates — yet RUN it and the colours wander, by pure copying-luck, until one is gone forever. Its sibling the Gene Jar (an infinite pool) never drifts; this one always does, and always ends in one colour — yet the fraction that end gold is exactly p.

1 · the living jar — one pool, drifting to monochrome

generation0
gold x = k/M0.50

statusdrifting
Click any bead to follow its lineage — watch one ancestor conquer the jar or vanish. M = 2N beads; each gen, every bead copies a random parent.

2 · the wall — a thousand jars, fixing toward two poles

sealed0 / 0
gold fixations—
ensemble mean x0.50
target p₀0.50
The gold share of the sealed jars homes onto p₀; the ensemble mean stays pinned at p₀ as the wall fans apart. Toggle N→∞ and the drift switches off.

Two views of one experiment. On the left, a single finite pool you watch wander to one colour — no selection, no mutation, just the lottery of which beads happen to get copied. On the right, a thousand of those jars run at once: each fixes to all-gold or all-slate, and the share that fix gold homes exactly onto p₀ — the martingale's promise, that drift spreads the ensemble but never shifts its centre. The mixedness H drains by 1−1/2N every generation. Take the pool to infinity and that factor becomes 1: the drain stops, nothing ever fixes, and you are back in the Gene Jar next door — the limit this jar can never quite reach.

↗ The Gene Jar — the infinite pool that never drifts (this jar’s N→∞ limit). ↗ The Selection Jar — the same finite drift, plus a seeing predator that aims it.

One law, three exact claims, re-run live in the self-test badge above: on the dense (2N+1)-state Wright–Fisher matrix the fixation probability equals the initial frequency (absorption uᵢ=i/M to the bit), the ensemble mean never drifts (a martingale), and the heterozygosity drains by exactly 1−1/2N per generation — with an N→∞ neg-control where drift switches off. The page’s core is the byte-twin of core.mjs; the Node test re-extracts it and proves the page === the module, and that the Gene Jar IS this jar’s infinite limit.
